newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed, foreign tranches down.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed, foreign tranches down.

text.p: Singapore shares ended mixed on Tuesday with the foreign tranches of banks and blue chips leading the fallers.
"Most of the local tranches of banks like DBS and UOB are up, but their foreign tranches are down," a broker with a Singapore firm said.
Dealers said the share movements could have been triggered by a local newspaper report pointing out the sharp premiums of foreign shares against their local tranches.
The foreign tranches of UOB and DBS fell 40 cents and 30 cents respectively to S$14.70 and S$18.30 while their local shares each gained 15 cents to S$8.45 and S$8.75.
The Straits Times Industrial Index ended 11.89 points down at 1,951.71. Total market volume was an active 268.55 million shares with 124 gainers against 258 losers.
The Jardine group of companies accounted for almost 40 percent of the volume and Hongkong Land topped the list with 54.65 million shares changing hands.
Those shares ended at US$3.12, up 57 cents after news that Cheung Kong of Hong Kong had accumulated more than three percent of the company.
"There is a lot of speculation that Cheung Kong could be mounting a takeover of the company again like they did in 1987," said one dealer.
Covered warrants of Hongkong Land also rocketted with the Robert Fleming covered warrant rising 191 percent, or US$0.335, to US$0.51.
Malaysian shares traded over the counter slid to new lows for the year with the UOB-OTC index touching 1,054.00 before ending at 1,054, down 6.75 points.
